text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Lithuania's loan for gas has reached 164 million litas and 76 million litas are to be paid immediately since Gazprom threatens to reduce the natural gas supply since February 1.Country's government issued a credit guarantee for $16 million to Hermis and Lithuanian Savings bank.
- World Bank will issue $20 million crdut to finance the reform of country's heath care system since Jan 1, 1998.
- The board of Bank of Lithuania decided on Thursday to liquidate Express bank.
- Lithuania does not want to reduce further the import tariffs for agricultural products.
- Lithuanian and Latvian customs officials will start working together in the Grenstale- Salociu check point on May 1.
- Japan opens its embassy in Vilnius on February 11. Lithuania can not reciprocate so far because of lack of funds.

- Lithuanian ambassador in Washington Alfonsas Eidintas expects to be re-called from his post after the top country officials critisized his work during annual meeting of diplomats in Vilnius this week.
- The well known American enviroment expert Valdas Adamkus will candidate during the municipalities' elections in March on the list of Centre Union in Siauliai.
- Estonian Savings Bank Hoiupank, with the approval of main shareholder, the EBRD, decided to acquire a controlling stake in one of three Lithuanian banks: Agricultural, Ukio or Litimpeks.
- The newspaper publishes 518 equity listings, the full list of shares registered on the stock exchange for potential investors to choose.
